beginner: A material in which charge can move readily.
precise: Has mobile charge carriers under an applied field.
misconception: It does not make current without a complete circuit and driving conditions.

beginner: A material that conducts very poorly in normal use.
precise: Carrier availability/mobility is low under stated conditions.
misconception: All insulators can fail under sufficiently high fields; not an absolute ban on conduction.

beginner: A material whose carriers can be controlled for useful electrical behavior.
precise: Its electronic states and band structure allow controllable carrier populations.
misconception: Doping does not turn an ordinary insulator into silicon; pure silicon already is a semiconductor.

beginner: An added atom that changes carrier behavior.
precise: An impurity species introduced to modify electronic carrier concentration.
misconception: A dopant is not a microscopic battery inside silicon.

beginner: Adding controlled impurities to a semiconductor.
precise: Changes carrier concentration and electrical characteristics.
misconception: It is not what originally makes pure silicon a semiconductor.

beginner: Semiconductor where electrons are the majority carriers.
precise: Donor doping increases electron population relative to holes.
misconception: The whole piece is not simply negatively charged.

beginner: Semiconductor where holes are the majority carriers.
precise: Acceptor doping increases hole population relative to electrons.
misconception: The whole piece is not simply positively charged.

beginner: A particle with negative electric charge.
precise: An elementary lepton described by quantum theory.
misconception: It is not a planet on a definite orbit and is not consumed as circuit fuel.

beginner: An effective positive carrier in a semiconductor.
precise: Missing occupation in valence electronic states behaves as a positive mobile carrier.
misconception: It is not a literal floating empty particle.

beginner: How fast net charge flows.
precise: Charge-flow rate through a cross-section, in amperes.
misconception: Signal speed is not the same as net electron drift speed.

beginner: Electric potential difference between points.
precise: Energy change per unit charge between locations.
misconception: A single point's voltage needs a reference.

beginner: An electrical influence that exerts force on charge.
precise: Electric force per unit positive test charge locally.
misconception: A MOSFET is controlled by a field, not a moving contact.

beginner: How a conductor/component limits current under stated conditions.
precise: Ratio of voltage to current at an operating point, with material/temperature dependence.
misconception: A resistor does not consume electrons.

beginner: A component designed to provide resistance.
precise: A part used for limiting current, voltage division and bias.
misconception: A resistor is not a semiconductor or transistor by definition.

beginner: How much separated charge a potential difference supports.
precise: Electrode charge magnitude divided by potential difference.
misconception: Capacitance is not the total net charge of both electrodes combined.

beginner: Conductors separated by an insulating dielectric.
precise: A component supporting opposite electrode charge and electric field energy.
misconception: It does not store free charge in the dielectric as a bucket.

beginner: A part whose current depends strongly on voltage direction.
precise: A general p-n diode's junction/bias controls carrier transport.
misconception: Reverse current is not identically zero under all conditions.

beginner: A light-emitting diode.
precise: A semiconductor device producing photons through suitable carrier recombination.
misconception: Color is not simply set by using more electricity.

beginner: A quantum of electromagnetic radiation, including light.
precise: An elementary field quantum with energy related to frequency.
misconception: It is not a tiny colored ball drawn to physical size.

beginner: A device that controls electrical conduction.
precise: A semiconductor device family used for amplification and switching.
misconception: Not every transistor is a MOSFET or a mechanical switch.

beginner: A transistor whose gate field controls a semiconductor channel.
precise: Metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistor; bias and polarity govern operation.
misconception: A gate HIGH does not mean ON for every polarity and source voltage.

beginner: A circuit implementing a logical input/output function.
precise: Interprets voltage ranges as logical states.
misconception: Logical zero/one are not identical to exact universal voltages.

beginner: Connected parts through which electrical effects act.
precise: Network of elements and nodes, including supply/return/control paths.
misconception: A drawing's arrows are not necessarily a series wire path.

beginner: Many electronic structures made together on a chip.
precise: Interconnected digital and/or analog circuits on a semiconductor die.
misconception: The black package is larger than the actual die and is not the die itself.

beginner: A chip combining a processor with memory and peripherals.
precise: An embedded computing device with programmable operation and I/O.
misconception: It is not just a CPU, and not all its blocks are logic gates.

beginner: A board supporting and connecting electronic parts.
precise: Printed circuit board with patterned conductors and insulating support.
misconception: The board substrate is not the same as its copper traces.

beginner: A patterned conductor on a PCB.
precise: A routed copper feature connecting nodes.
misconception: It is not an abstract signal arrow with zero electrical properties.

beginner: A conductive connection area for a lead or contact.
precise: PCB land associated with mounting/connection/test access.
misconception: A pad need not be a via or a plated hole.

beginner: A connection between board copper layers.
precise: A plated interlayer feature defined in the board design.
misconception: Not every mounting hole is a via.

beginner: Software programmed into an embedded device.
precise: Executable/data content used by hardware for its operation.
misconception: Firmware is information, not literally a physical collection of gates.

beginner: A program that helps load another program.
precise: Firmware managing program transfer/storage and startup under configured conditions.
misconception: It is not the USB bridge chip itself.

beginner: Encoded instructions a processor can execute.
precise: Binary instruction encodings for a specific architecture.
misconception: High-level statements do not each map to one universal instruction.
